1.why: Every MFA route resolves the account from the server-side session (owned()), and the object() guard even rejects bodies containing id/accountId/userId fields, so only the session owner's settings are touched.

2.why: Verification codes are stored as a salted hash on the individual session's challenge object, so a code issued to one session/user cannot be used by another.

3.why: At sign-in all existing sessions for the account are deleted ('for (const [id, session] of sessions) ... sessions.delete(id)'), so no previous sessions survive to persist after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted (encrypt()/account.secret) and recovery codes are stored as salted SHA-256 hashes, never in plain text.

5.why: All secrets, identity codes, recovery codes, session ids and CSRF tokens are generated with crypto.getRandomValues, a CSPRNG.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used (codes live only in JS memory), and the session cookie is HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Strict; only the non-secret login CSRF token sits in a non-HttpOnly cookie.

7.why: Server-side validators (emailOK, passwordOK, otpOK, recoveryOK) plus the strict object() body check validate all input; data lives in in-memory Maps so there is no SQL injection surface.

8.why: Dynamic values are rendered via textContent or the esc() helper, server messages are inserted with textContent, and a strict nonce-based CSP blocks any injected script execution.

9.why: Client navigation is restricted to a fixed routes allowlist defaulting to #signin, and the server rejects any request body containing 'next' or 'redirect', so no open redirect exists.

10.why: secureHeaders() sets CSP (with frame-ancestors 'none'), HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY and more on every response including errors.

11.why: sessionCookie() emits 'HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' on the mfa_session cookie.

12.why: Server keeps secrets out of logs, URLs and error output and returns only generic 500s without stack traces, though the demo deliberately console.logs simulated OTPs/recovery codes in the browser via privateDemo().

13.why: Identity challenges expire after 15 minutes and are marked used on success, TOTP time-steps are recorded in usedSteps for single-use, and recovery codes carry a used flag.

14.why: Identity, authenticator and recovery verification each lock the account for 10 minutes after 5 failed attempts (identityFails/authFails/recoveryFails with clearLock).

15.why: Sign-in issues a fresh random session id while deleting all prior sessions, getSession enforces 30-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session and expires the cookie.
